+# named by the PR fixture's head.diff headers (`diff --git a/X b/Y` both names, quoted C-style names
+# unquoted, `--- a/X`, `+++ b/Y`, `rename from|to X`; /dev/null and unsafe paths dropped) or present under
+# its head/ or base/ tree. Over transcripts/events-{BARE,REVIEW,AUDIT}.jsonl each assistant tool_use is
+# correlated with its tool_result by id. Paths are resolved against the session's cwd (the system init
+# event's, default /workspace, which is also the workspace root), `cd DIR` segments, NAME=value
+# assignments (H=pr/head) and `for V in w…; do` lists; a path inside the workspace and outside pr/ is a
+# workspace operand, pr/head/X and pr/base/X are PR operands.
+#   diff form — a Bash segment (split on newline, ; && || | & outside quotes and parentheses; heredoc bodies
+#   removed first) whose executable is diff, sdiff or comm, or git with diff and --no-index, without -q
+#   (alone or in a short-flag cluster), --brief or --quiet, holding a PR operand and a workspace operand that
+#   names an answer path (or a directory above one); a head.diff operand is never a PR operand. Its result
+#   is split into per-file sections at `diff `, `--- ` and `*** ` header lines (text no header attributes
+#   goes to every target of the command); unified `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` and normal `NaM,b` / `N,Mc…` / `Nd…`
+#   ranges are read (head side, below); a planted site of that file within ±3 of a range, or its must_match
+#   text (stripped, first 50 characters, at least 12) in the section, marks the defect exposed (how diff);
+#   a non-empty section that is not only error lines and yields neither ranges nor must_match marks every
+#   other defect of that file exposed_unknown. Text no header attributes, in a command with several
+#   targets, exposes a defect only with corroboration: a range near the site AND a line of the fixture's
+#   head/X within ±3 of the site in that text, or must_match. A diff whose output is discarded or reduced
+#   (>/dev/null, | wc, | grep -c|-q|-l, | cmp) and a tool_result flagged is_error print no content.

+#   Read (file_path) / Grep (path) tool_use, naming a workspace answer path (a directory for grep or Grep
+#   covers the answer paths below it), whose result contains a LATER-ONLY line within ±3 of a planted site

+# Ranges are read on the head side only: planted sites are head coordinates, so the side of the pr/head

+ORACLE_PHASES = ("BARE", "REVIEW", "AUDIT")
+DIFF_EXE = {"diff", "sdiff", "comm"}
+READ_EXE = {"cat", "sed", "awk", "grep", "head", "tail", "less", "python3"}

+                      r"No such file|Is a directory|hook error|BLOCKED|^\s*$|^\s*(?:rc|exit)\s*=\s*\d+\s*$")
+DIFF_BODY = re.compile(r"^[<>+\- @\\0-9]|^---$")
+FILEISH = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+|[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}\b")
+# a diff whose stdout is counted, tested or discarded prints no content: | wc, | grep -c/-q/-l, >/dev/null
+SILENT_SINK = re.compile(r"^(?:wc|cmp|true|false|test)\b|^grep\s+(?:-[A-Za-z]*[cql][A-Za-z]*|--count|--quiet|--files-with-matches)\b")

+def unquote_c(q):
+    """a git C-quoted path body (between the quotes) → text"""
+    i, b = 0, bytearray()
+    while i < len(q):
+        ch = q[i]
+        if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(q):
+            n = q[i + 1]
+            if n in "01234567" and re.match(r"[0-7]{3}", q[i + 1:i + 4]):
+                b.append(int(q[i + 1:i + 4], 8))
+                i += 4
+                continue
+            b.extend({"n": b"\n", "t": b"\t", '"': b'"', "\\": b"\\"}.get(n, n.encode()))
+            i += 2
+            continue
+        b.extend(ch.encode())
+        i += 1
+    return b.decode("utf-8", "replace")
+

+def answer_paths(pr):
+    names = set()
+    text = read_regular(os.path.join(pr, "head.diff"), 64 * 1024 * 1024, root=pr) or ""
+    Q = r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"'
+    for line in text.split("\n"):
+        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
+            rest = line[len("diff --git "):]
+            m = re.fullmatch(Q.replace("((", "a/((", 1) + " " + Q.replace("((", "b/((", 1), rest) or None
+            if m:
+                names.update(unquote_c(x) for x in m.groups())
+                continue
+            m = re.fullmatch(r"a/(\S+) b/(\S+)", rest)
+            if m:
+                names.update(m.groups())
+                continue
+            half = (len(rest) - 1) // 2   # unquoted names with spaces: "a/X b/X" with X twice
+            if rest[:2] == "a/" and rest[half + 1:half + 3] == "b/" and rest[2:half] == rest[half + 3:]:
+                names.add(rest[2:half])
+        elif line.startswith(("--- ", "+++ ")):
+            body = line[4:].split("\t", 1)[0]
+            if body.startswith('"') and body.endswith('"'):
+                body = unquote_c(body[1:-1])
+            if body.startswith(("a/", "b/")):
+                names.add(body[2:])
+        elif line.startswith(("rename from ", "rename to ", "copy from ", "copy to ")):
+            body = line.split(" ", 2)[2]
+            names.add(unquote_c(body[1:-1]) if body.startswith('"') and body.endswith('"') else body)
+    for side in ("head", "base"):
+        root = os.path.join(pr, side)
+        for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root):
+            for n in fs:
+                names.add(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r, n), root).replace(os.sep, "/"))
+    out = set()
+    for n in names:
+        parts = safe_rel(n)
+        if parts and n != "/dev/null":
+            rel = "/".join(parts)
+            if rel.startswith(ANSWER_TOP):
+                out.add(rel)
+    return out

+def split_segments(cmd):
+    """[(segment, separator after it)]: split on newline ; & | (&& || included) outside quotes and
+    parentheses; the separator is "|" for a pipe into the next segment, else ";" """
+    segs, cur, q, depth, i = [], [], None, 0, 0
+    while i < len(cmd):
+        ch = cmd[i]
+        if q == "'":
+            cur.append(ch)
+            if ch == "'":
+                q = None
+        elif q == '"':
+            cur.append(ch)
+            if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(cmd):
+                cur.append(cmd[i + 1])
+                i += 1
+            elif ch == '"':
+                q = None
+        elif ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(cmd):
+            cur.append(ch + cmd[i + 1])
+            i += 1
+        elif ch in "'\"":
+            q = ch
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif ch == "(":
+            depth += 1

content.content:
+            depth += 1
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif ch == ")":
+            depth = max(0, depth - 1)
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif depth == 0 and ch in "\n;&|":
+            pipe = ch == "|" and cmd[i + 1:i + 2] != "|" and cmd[i - 1:i] != "|"
+            segs.append(("".join(cur), "|" if pipe else ";"))
+            cur = []
+        else:

+def seg_words(seg):

+def expand(tok, vars_):
+    """$NAME / ${NAME} expansion → list of strings (a loop variable expands to every word); an unknown
+    variable leaves the token unresolved (dropped)"""
+    outs = [tok]
+    for _ in range(4):
+        nxt, changed = [], False
+        for o in outs:
+            m = re.search(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}|\$([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", o)
+            if not m:
+                nxt.append(o)
+                continue
+            name = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
+            if name not in vars_:
+                continue
+            changed = True
+            for v in vars_[name]:
+                nxt.append(o[:m.start()] + v + o[m.end():])
+        outs = nxt
+        if not changed:
+            break
+    return [o for o in outs if "$" not in o]

+def classify(tok, cwd, ws):
+    """→ ("pr", side, rel) | ("ws", rel) | None"""
+    tok = tok.strip("'\"")
+    if not tok or tok.startswith("-") or "://" in tok:
+        return None
+    if tok.startswith("~") or "*" in tok or "?" in tok:
+        return None
+    full = os.path.normpath(tok if tok.startswith("/") else os.path.join(cwd, tok))
+    if full != ws and not full.startswith(ws.rstrip("/") + "/"):
+        return None
+    rel = "" if full == ws else full[len(ws.rstrip("/")) + 1:]
+    if rel == "pr" or rel.startswith("pr/"):
+        rest = rel[3:]
+        for side in ("head", "base"):
+            if rest == side or rest.startswith(side + "/"):
+                return ("pr", side, rest[len(side) + 1:])
+        return ("pr", None, rest)
+    return ("ws", rel)

+def ws_targets(rel, answer, directory_ok):
+    if rel in answer:
+        return [rel]
+    if not directory_ok:
+        return []
+    pre = "" if rel in ("", ".") else rel.rstrip("/") + "/"
+    return sorted(a for a in answer if a.startswith(pre))

+def segment_tokens(seg, vars_, cwd, ws):
+    """every path-shaped token of a segment (inside process substitutions too), expanded and classified"""
+    out = []
+    for m in PATHISH.finditer(seg):
+        for v in expand(m.group(0), vars_):
+            c = classify(v, cwd, ws)
+            if c is not None:

+    return out

+def result_text(blk):
+    c = blk.get("content")
+    if isinstance(c, str):
+        return c
+    if isinstance(c, list):
+        return "\n".join(x.get("text", "") for x in c if isinstance(x, dict) and isinstance(x.get("text"), str))

+def ranges_of(text, sides=("left", "right")):
+    """the printed line ranges of a unified or normal diff on the given sides (left = first operand)"""
+    rs = []
+    for m in HUNK_U.finditer(text):
+        a, n = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2) or 1)
+        c, k = int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4) or 1)
+        if "left" in sides:
+            rs.append((a, a + max(n, 1) - 1))
+        if "right" in sides:
+            rs.append((c, c + max(k, 1) - 1))
+    for m in HUNK_N.finditer(text):
+        a = int(m.group(1))
+        c = int(m.group(4))
+        if "left" in sides:
+            rs.append((a, int(m.group(2) or a)))
+        if "right" in sides:
+            rs.append((c, int(m.group(5) or c)))
+    return rs

+def sections(text, targets):
+    """{target: [section body]}: the result split at header lines — a diff header (diff, ---, +++, ***) or
+    a line that is not diff body and names a file (an `echo "=== $f"` marker); a header naming a target
+    (the longest one it holds) opens that target's section, any other header a dropped one; text before
+    the first header belongs to the sole target. Text no header attributes (several targets) is returned
+    as the loose list. Header lines are not part of a body. → (sections, loose)"""
+    out = {f: [] for f in targets}
+    loose = []
+    cur = targets[0] if len(targets) == 1 else None
+    buf = []
+
+    def flush():
+        if buf:
+            (out[cur] if cur is not None else loose).append("\n".join(buf))
+
+    for line in text.split("\n"):
+        diff_hdr = line.startswith(("diff ", "--- ", "*** ", "+++ "))
+        if diff_hdr or (not DIFF_BODY.match(line) and FILEISH.search(line)):
+            named = sorted((f for f in targets if f in line), key=len, reverse=True)
+            hit = named[0] if named else None
+            if line.startswith("+++ ") and hit == cur:
+                continue
+            if hit is not None or diff_hdr or len(targets) > 1:
+                flush()
+                buf = []
+                cur = hit
+                continue
+        buf.append(line)
+    flush()
+    return out, loose

+import hashlib, os, re, shutil, stat, subprocess, sys
+
+def note(msg):
+    sys.stderr.write("sandbox-mount: " + msg + "\n")
+
+def die(msg, code=2):
+    note(msg)
+    sys.exit(code)
+
+def sha(b):
+    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
+
+def git(repo, *args):
+    env = {"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin"), "HOME": "/nonexistent", "LC_ALL": "C",
+           "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": "/dev/null", "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1", "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0",
+           "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0"}

+    try:
+        p = subprocess.run(cmd, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+                           env=env, timeout=300)
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+    return p.stdout if p.returncode == 0 else None
+
+def has_commit(repo, c):
+    return bool(c) and git(repo, "cat-file", "-e", c + "^{commit}") is not None
+
+def norm(p):
+    if not p or p.startswith("/") or "\\" in p or any(ord(ch) < 32 or ord(ch) == 127 for ch in p):
+        return None
+    parts = p.split("/")
+    if any(x in ("", ".", "..") for x in parts):
+        return None
+    return "/".join(parts)

+ESC = {"a": 7, "b": 8, "t": 9, "n": 10, "v": 11, "f": 12, "r": 13, '"': 34, "\\": 92}
+
+def take_quoted(s):
+    """s starts with a double quote: returns (unquoted, rest) or (None, s)."""
+    out = bytearray(); i = 1
+    while i < len(s):
+        c = s[i]
+        if c == '"':

+        if c == "\\" and i + 1 < len(s):
+            n = s[i + 1]
+            if n in ESC:

+            if re.match(r"[0-7]{3}", s[i + 1:i + 4]):
+                out.append(int(s[i + 1:i + 4], 8) & 0xFF); i += 4; continue
+            out.extend(n.encode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")); i += 2; continue
+        out.extend(c.encode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")); i += 1
+    return None, s

+    if s.startswith('"'):

+        return v
+    return s

+    if p.startswith("a/") or p.startswith("b/"):

+    return p

+    names = []
+    if rest.startswith('"'):
+        a, tail = take_quoted(rest)
+        if a is None:
+            return []
+        tail = tail.lstrip(" ")
+        b = one_name(tail)
+        return [a, b]
+    if ' "b/' in rest:
+        i = rest.index(' "b/')
+        return [rest[:i], one_name(rest[i + 1:])]
+    n = len(rest)
+    if n >= 5 and (n - 5) % 2 == 0:
+        L = (n - 5) // 2
+        if rest.startswith("a/") and rest[2 + L:5 + L] == " b/" and rest[2:2 + L] == rest[5 + L:]:
+            return ["a/" + rest[2:2 + L], "b/" + rest[5 + L:]]
+    if " b/" in rest:
+        i = rest.index(" b/")
+        return [rest[:i], rest[i + 1:]]
+    return names
+
+def diff_paths(diff_file):
+    raw = open(diff_file, "rb").read().decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")
+    out = []
+    old_left = new_left = 0
+    for line in raw.split("\n"):
+        if line.endswith("\r"):
+            line = line[:-1]
+        if old_left > 0 or new_left > 0:
+            if line.startswith("\\"):
+                continue
+            c = line[:1]
+            if c == " " or line == "":
+                old_left -= 1; new_left -= 1; continue
+            if c == "-":
+                old_left -= 1; continue
+            if c == "+":
+                new_left -= 1; continue

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}

+  done

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

Several toggles rewrite files under .claude/: effort (a7_effort_medium, task_types all) strips `effort:` from every .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md and edits .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml, rule_files deletes .claude/rules/*.md, and audit_delta_instruction edits auditing-security/SKILL.md. On any review-catch fixture whose answer set includes one of those files (gate SKILL.md files are named explicitly as answer paths), clause (c) `mount_mutated` fails and every trial of that arm becomes infrastructure_error. Even if the check passed, the sandbox would no longer hold the PR's version. Either run the toggles before the overlay and record the hashes afterwards, or have the toggles skip answer paths. No test covers a toggle combined with an overlaid SKILL.md.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:478 — dissent_absent_reason maps every envelope status other than budget_exceeded, *preflight* and failed (or a record-fallback) to "none" ("the dissent ran"). adversarial-review.sh writes metadata.status "api_failure" and "malformed_response" when the dissent produced nothing, and "skipped_by_config" when it was disabled by something other than the sandbox YAML. Those gates read as "none", so the "dissent-absent gates excluded" sensitivity in the report never removes the most common unplanned absence: an API failure.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1153 — part_split adds "· rule <r>" to every row's key once review rows carry two grader rules. Build rows have no rule, so they go to their own "· rule n/a" partition, away from both review partitions. No partition then holds both build (hidden_test_pass_rate) and review-catch (defect_catch_rate) rows. The primary (the largest partition, usually the build rows) loses its catch-rate H1 read, and the review partitions lose the pass-rate read. A grader-rule split should only partition the review-catch rows. The c131-mixed fixture changes pin and rule together, so this case is untested.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1656 — missed_pm3_v1 ids missing from the current key are mapped to their position in the v1 manifest. When the curated manifest has dropped or reordered defects, that "dN" can collide with a different current defect's position. The same lists then go through ablation-row's poslist against the current defects_seeded, so a v1-only position beyond the current count makes the whole field null.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:717 — defect_vector for defect_catch_rate_pm3_v1 builds a vector of the CURRENT manifest's length (task_defects) from the v1 missed list. A defect that exists only in the current manifest is never in missed_pm3_v1, so it counts as caught (1.0). When the v1 and curated defect sets differ, the beside figure disagrees with the row's own recall_pm3_v1 (computed over planted_v1). That breaks the claim that "recall_pm3_v1 reproduces a 1.2.x grade".
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135 — when EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset and <manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head does not exist, the same-scope clause and the citation-validity line count fall back to <workspace>/pr/head. ablation-grade.sh copies the agent-writable sandbox pr/ into the grading workspace (ablation-grade.sh:2624) and leaves EVAL_HEAD_DIR unset whenever resolve_pr_fixture fails (ablation-grade.sh:1634). The agent could then rewrite the head file to change definition scopes or line counts and earn credits, which contradicts the documented "never the agent-writable sandbox pr/". The grader should refuse the scope clause rather than read the workspace copy.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:381 — evidence_line takes the FIRST copy_source= line, but pipeline-run.sh checks the LAST one (`sed -n '$p'`). If the evidence ever holds two lines (for example, a re-materialisation), the pre-launch and post-run checks look at different values.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:77 — oracle_closed is added only to a1_full's took_effect. a3_one_voice and a7_effort_medium are also mounted review-catch arms that get the closed mount, but nothing checks after the run that their mount stayed closed (clauses (b)-(d), mount_mutated). The PR states that every mounted review-catch arm runs the closed mount.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1643 — the example config now writes `budget_scale: fixed` (and again at line 1707). Anyone who copies the example gets CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET=true, which changes the envelope (budget_scale, budget_cents_effective and budget_cents_max in metadata, plus `reason` on budget_exceeded). This contradicts the documented "an absent key is the shipped gate, byte for byte". Leave the keys commented out in the example.
head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:4445 — the budget_exceeded envelope gains `metadata.reason: "budget"`, but adversarial-finding.schema.json's metadata block (additionalProperties: false; the new properties end at line 258) does not declare `reason`. The schema also has no `maximum` on anchor_line / anchor_line_end, although the normaliser enforces 10,000,000.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2010 — corpus_sha256 checks the file with the symlink-refusing, size-capped read_regular, then reopens the same path with a plain open() and hashes that. The digest therefore follows symlinks and is not bounded by the same read (a TOCTOU gap). It should hash the bytes from the bounded read.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:984 — precision_planted_per_flag (defects caught ÷ findings flagged) is labelled a precision, but under the same-scope rule one citation can credit several defects, so it can exceed 1 (the AR-52 fixture asserts 1.5). It should be named a ratio, not a precision.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 12 findings and a verdict of **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. I read the code and didn't run any tests; nothing under `pr/` was changed.

The three that block the merge:

1. **The arm toggles undo the closed mount** (`pipeline-run.sh:566`). The PR's overlay writes and fingerprints the PR's version of the review-catch files first. The arm toggles then rewrite files under `.claude/`: `effort` strips `effort:` from every `SKILL.md`, `rule_files` deletes rule files, and `audit_delta_instruction` edits a `SKILL.md`. The pre-launch check then compares against the fingerprints taken before the toggles. On any review-catch PR that touches one of those files, the check reports `mount_mutated`, and every `a7_effort_medium` trial (or any arm with such a toggle) is refused as an infrastructure error.
2. **API failures count as "the dissent ran"** (`ablation-row.sh:478`). The new dissent-absent reason only recognises `budget_exceeded`, preflight and `failed`. The adversarial review script also writes `api_failure`, `malformed_response` and `skipped_by_config`, and those all read as "none". So the "dissent-absent gates excluded" sensitivity never removes the most common unplanned absence.
3. **A grader-rule split separates build rows from review rows** (`ablation-report.py:1153`). When review rows carry two grader rules, build rows (which have no rule) land in their own partition. No partition then holds both the pass-rate and catch-rate rows, so H1 loses one of its reads. The mixed test fixture changes the commit and the rule together, so this case is never exercised.

The other findings, in brief:
- **v1 positions:** they are mapped against the current manifest in the grader and the report. When the curated and v1 defect sets differ, positions can collide and the `pm3_v1` figure gets inflated. That breaks the claim that it reproduces a 1.2.x grade.
- **Grader falls back to the agent's copy:** when the fixture's `head/` can't be found, the same-scope rule reads `<workspace>/pr/head`. In the ablation grader that is a copy of the agent-writable sandbox.
- **Post-run check covers one arm only:** only `a1_full` gets `oracle_closed`, though the other mounted review-catch arms also run the closed mount.
- **Example config changes the envelope:** `.loa.config.yaml.example` now writes `budget_scale: fixed`. Anyone who copies it gets the new envelope fields, contradicting "an absent key is the shipped gate".
- **Smaller issues:**
  - The schema doesn't declare the new `reason` field and has no upper limit on `anchor_line`.
  - `corpus_sha256` reads the file safely, then hashes it through a second, unguarded open.
  - The two mount checks read different `copy_source` lines (first vs last).
  - `precision_planted_per_flag` can exceed 1 (the fixture asserts 1.5), so it shouldn't be called a precision.
